name: Punctate Acrokeratoderma with Freckle-like Pigmentation

criteria.description: Presence of multiple punctate hyperkeratotic papules on acral sites with freckle-like pigmentation
Skin biopsy showing focal hyperkeratosis with epidermal acanthosis and pigment incontinence
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical lesions plus supportive histopathological findings
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is not routinely available; diagnosis is primarily clinical and histological.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple punctate hyperkeratotic papules on palms and soles
pathognomonic.notes: Lesions are typically small, discrete, and localized to acral surfaces.
searchTerms: multiple small thickened bumps on palms and soles
punctate hyperkeratotic papules on hands and feet
tiny rough spots on palms and soles

pathognomonic.symptomName: Freckle-like brownish pigmentation on acral skin
pathognomonic.notes: Pigmentation often co-localizes with hyperkeratotic papules.
searchTerms: freckle-like brown spots on hands and feet
small brown skin spots on acral areas
freckled pigmentation on fingers and toes

common.symptomName: Mild pruritus localized to affected areas
common.notes: Itching may increase with sweating or heat.
searchTerms: localized mild itching on affected skin
itching limited to thickened areas
slight pruritus in keratoderma regions

common.symptomName: Symmetrical distribution of lesions on palms and soles
searchTerms: skin lesions evenly spread on palms and soles
symmetrical spots on hands and feet
matching skin patches on both palms and soles

common.symptomName: Onset during childhood or early adulthood
searchTerms: symptoms start in childhood or young adulthood
early life onset of signs
beginning during childhood or early adult years
no general symptoms
absence of systemic signs
no widespread illness symptoms

occasional.notes: Fissures may cause discomfort but are usually superficial.

slight fissures in rough skin
small splits in hardened skin areas

occasional.notes: Erythema may be induced by friction or heat.
searchTerms: temporary redness around lesions
brief skin erythema near spots
transient skin redness
short-term red skin flare
excessive sweating on hands and feet
palm and sole sweating

occasional.notes: Scaling is usually minimal and localized.

rare.symptomName: Secondary bacterial infection of fissured lesions
rare.notes: Infections are uncommon but may occur with fissures.
searchTerms: bacterial infection in cracked skin lesions

rare.symptomName: Extension of pigmentation beyond acral sites
rare.notes: Rarely pigmentation may involve dorsal hands or feet.

rare.symptomName: Nail dystrophy associated with acral lesions
rare.notes: Nail changes are infrequent and mild.
searchTerms: nail abnormalities with acral skin lesions

genetic: No specific gene identified; possible autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: Histopathology: focal hyperkeratosis, acanthosis, pigment incontinence

distinguishingFeatures: Larger keratotic papules without freckle-like pigmentation
Onset in adulthood with history of exposure or trauma

redFlags: Rapid progression of pigmentation or lesions
Presence of ulceration or bleeding in lesions
Systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
